restitution.src: e = exp(-pi zeta / sqrt(1 - zeta^2)) from the damping ratios below

collision_thickness_mm.src: internal layer; small offset for fascia planes (E)

loss_factor_impact.src: from deform.viscoelastic (SOFTTISSUE M30/M31; VANLOOCKE09). A ms-scale muscle Prony set was not found: muscle under a slap is stiffer than its quasi-static law by ~4-5x already at 80 Hz. how a solver uses it: integrate the Prony set (deform.viscoelastic.prony) as internal variables in an implicit step (one exponential update per term per step; stable at any dt) on top of the hyperelastic stress, so a 1-10 ms slap sees the short-time stiffness and loses energy in the 1-10 ms terms; do not use Rayleigh damping fitted to the ~15 Hz wobble: beta-damping gives zeta = beta * omega / 2, so a beta set for zeta 0.15 at 15 Hz (beta 3.2 ms) gives zeta ~5 at 250-500 Hz (a 1-2 ms pulse): over-damped, the slap goes dead. Where only one number fits, use the loss factor at the pulse's frequency f ~ 1 / (2 x contact time), zeta = tan_delta / 2.

contact_stiffness_kPa_per_mm.src: per region: set by the stack in the skin profile

strain_stiffening.src: SOFTTISSUE section 3 from R31's gluteal muscle points

model.src: MORROW10 along / across fibre ~20:1 in tension

density_kg_m3.src: MENDEZ60 fresh mammalian 1.0597; ICRU44 1.05; fixed human 1.112 (WARD05) (the project's materials research note GAPS_RESEARCH.md 3)

poisson.src: nu = (3K - 2G) / (2 (3K + G)), K 2.6 GPa, G 4 kPa -> 0.49999; 0.4992 a solver-safe stand-in (E inside D)

anisotropy.src: MORROW10 rabbit EDL tension (~20:1); compression can reverse it (Takaza 2013, unverified) (the project's materials research note GAPS_RESEARCH.md 3)

ogden.src: not found for human muscle in this pass

prony.src: VANLOOCKE09 Table 2, NLV-SYM model fitted to 10 % cycles at 0.4 Hz, porcine; slow terms only (0.6-300 s): seconds-scale relaxation, NOT impact; weights valid inside that model (strain-dependent multipliers h, a), and the authors report it misses the stiffening above 5 Hz

dynamic_stiffening_vs_freq.src: VANLOOCKE09: stress-cycle amplitude of 10 % cycles at 25 % mean compression rises ~4.1x (abstract) to ~5x (text) from 0.22 to 80 Hz (5 to 3200 %strain/s); cross-fibre 1.2x stiffer at low amplitude; porcine, ex vivo

high_rate_E_kPa.src: keys: strain rate per s; values: dynamic stiffness relative to 0.05 /s (no absolute E retrieved): VANLOOCKE09 cycle-amplitude ratio at 0.22 Hz (5 %/s) vs 80 Hz (3200 %/s). Times the quasi-static law (deform.stiffening) for a first estimate

high_rate_compression.v: concave-up, strongly rate-sensitive stress-strain in compression at Hopkinson-bar rates: bovine 1000-2500 /s to 80 % strain (VANSLIGT06); porcine 0.007-3700 /s, along and across fibre (SONG07); human soleus / gastrocnemius ~500-1800 /s, stiffer than porcine and bovine, rate effect evident above ~150 /s, soleus stiffer (BALARAMAN). Numbers only in figures: not digitised

loss_factor_vs_freq.src: tan_delta ~ 2 zeta from the in vivo segment wobble (SOFTTISSUE M31 thigh zeta 0.11-0.16 at 14-16 Hz; M30 calf 0.42 at 10.5 Hz): a whole-segment mode (muscle + fat + skin, activation-dependent), not a material loss factor; 100 and 1000 Hz not found (MRE G'' for thigh muscle not retrieved)

loss_vs_freq_measured.src: Voigt fits to in vivo human shear-wave phase-velocity dispersion: GENNISSON10 Table 1 and 3 (supersonic shear imaging, brachialis, 100-800 Hz, volunteer 1 for the loads) and HOYT08 Table 2 and 3 (crawling-wave sonoelastography, 80-200 Hz, along fibres, 2 men) (mu, eta: M); tan delta = 2 pi f eta / mu computed here (D). The two disagree ~14x along the fibre at 100 Hz (0.07 vs 0.7-1.3): GENNISSON10 found the along-fibre wave nearly non-dispersive (low eta) and the across-fibre wave strongly dispersive; the Voigt model forces tan delta to grow linearly with f, and GENNISSON10 note it was not validated against attenuation. HOYT08 values at 300 and 1000 Hz and GENNISSON10 at 1000 Hz are past their bands (extrapolated). For a slap on relaxed muscle (shear across the fibres under the skin) the across-fibre SSI case is the closest measured: tan delta ~0.4 at 100 Hz, ~1 at 300 Hz. Contraction raises mu ~7-17x and eta ~4-10x along the fibre
loss_vs_freq_measured.method: in vivo ultrasound shear-wave elastography dispersion (SSI 100-800 Hz; crawling waves 80-200 Hz), Kelvin-Voigt fit

G_storage_loss_vs_freq_measured_kPa.src: Voigt: G' = mu, G'' = 2 pi f eta, from GENNISSON10 Table 1 (0 kg) and HOYT08 Table 2/3 relaxed; computed here; values past each band extrapolated

stiffening.form: E_t(eps) = E0 * exp(k * (eps - eps_ref)): tangent compressive modulus, relaxed muscle, quasi-static, in vivo, whole layer in place

E0_kPa.src: ISOGAI22 (SOFTTISSUE R31) gluteal muscle in vivo, E at 5 N (strain 0.19) 62.2 +/- 10.3 kPa, relaxed

stiffening.src: ISOGAI22 via SOFTTISSUE R31 / section 3; contraction raises G x2.6 and more (SOFTTISSUE R28-R30), not in this law
